nouns.name: bulldocs
nouns.summary: Bulldocs — live, no-reload paper/document surface. Ingests block-structured papers from external producers and renders them at /papers/:slug with real-time per-block streaming. Formerly the built-in Papers feature; now a first-party plugin built on the core portable-doc utilities.

nouns.name: fleet
nouns.summary: Tasks — the W7 task-document substrate as a first-party plugin. Declares the `task` schema (goals/phases/events are all just tasks) and owns the TTL-sweep + compaction Oban cron jobs. Built on the core Barkpark.Tasks machinery, which stays in core as reusable utilities.

nouns.name: github
nouns.summary: GitHub bridge — Barkpark (the guerrilla ledger) stays the single source of truth; this plugin mirrors tasks OUTBOUND to GitHub Issues (debounced, idempotent, App-authenticated), intakes only outsider-opened issues INBOUND as find-or-create tasks awaiting adoption, and projects a READ-ONLY Projects v2 dashboard. No field is ever bidirectional; claims/epochs/fencing/rail_rev never leave Barkpark. Off by default.

nouns.name: onixedit
nouns.summary: ONIX 3.0 book metadata editor — Norwegian-publisher flavoured. Phase 4 skeleton (WI1) — book schema surface only; contributor / Thema / localizedText shapes are filled in by WI2 and codelist seeding lands in WI3.

nouns.name: task
nouns.summary: Tasks — the W7 task-document substrate as a first-party plugin. Declares the `task` schema (goals/phases/events are all just tasks) and owns the TTL-sweep + compaction Oban cron jobs. Built on the core Barkpark.Tasks machinery, which stays in core as reusable utilities.

nouns.name: ticket
nouns.summary: Tickets — possession of a NAMED api key is identity. An operator mints a named low-trust key and hands it to an outside user; the key-holder files tickets (requests/questions, optionally with media) that live as type-`ticket` documents with an embedded append-only message thread; the operator answers from Studio/CLI, and the key-holder retrieves the answer with the SAME key. Status IS the turn indicator (open = operator's move, answered = submitter's move, closed = done; a submitter reply auto-reopens).

nouns.name: ticket-key
nouns.summary: Tickets — possession of a NAMED api key is identity. Status IS the turn indicator (open = operator's move, answered = submitter's move, closed = done; a submitter reply auto-reopens).

commands.summary: Close a claimed task by id; --set 'criteria:=[…]' updates acceptance criteria in the same atomic write (omitted evidence preserves the stored value; evidence:"" clears it). By default fences on a claim-time work digest: if the task's brief (title/description/acceptance_criteria) changed under your claim, the close 409s doc_changed_since_claim and the response names current_rev + changed_fields. To recover: re-read the task, reconcile those changed fields, then close with that current_rev via --set observed_rev=<current_rev> (strict full-rev CAS, bypasses the digest fence). A plain re-read is NOT enough — a same-worker re-read preserves the claim-time work digest, so closing again without observed_rev repeats the same 409.

flags.name: set
flags.summary: Extra close-body fields as key=value (key:=json for typed). The expectation close-out (task-proves-paper): --set 'criteria:=[{"index":0,"met":true,"evidence":"PR #1234","criterion":"<the criterion's exact stored wording>"}]' flips acceptance_criteria met/evidence atomically with the close (same rev CAS — no separate racing mutation). "criterion" is REQUIRED on every entry with met=true: the 0-based index alone is unverifiable, so an unguarded met-flip is REJECTED (409 criterion_text_required) rather than silently flipping a neighbouring criterion, and a text that does not match the row at that index is REJECTED too (409 criteria_mismatch). An entry with met=false needs no text. Optional evidence is presence-sensitive: omit the key to preserve stored evidence, or send evidence:"" to clear it. A done close over unmet criteria is REFUSED (409 criteria_unmet, 0-based indices); close over them on the record with --set criteria_override="<why it is done anyway>" (recorded as close_override.criteria; met stays false); cancelled and blocked are exempt by name; a non-holder close is 409 not_holder unless --set holder_override="<reason>". --set observed_rev=<rev> pins the strict full-rev CAS and BYPASSES the default work-digest fence (use when you intend to close against the exact rev you read).

flags.name: observed_rail_rev
flags.summary: The rail_rev (rail ETag) you last observed for this task's parent rail. When it differs from the current rail_rev the response carries a rail_changed notice — advisory, never a gate.

commands.summary: Stamp ONE acceptance criterion mid-claim: --criterion N (N is the ZERO-BASED index — the first criterion is 0, NOT 1) with either --met --evidence "…" (flips the lock; evidence is REQUIRED, non-empty) or --miss --note "…" (records the honest attempt on the criterion's attempts list — bounded to the 5 most recent — WITHOUT flipping met). --met ALSO REQUIRES --criterion-text "<the criterion's exact stored wording>": the index alone is unverifiable, so an unguarded met-flip is REJECTED (409 criterion_text_required) rather than silently flipping whatever row the index lands on. If the text does not match the row at N the stamp is REJECTED too (409 criteria_mismatch) — nothing is written. --miss needs no text (it flips nothing). Holder-only + the same epoch fence as close (a lapsed claim can't stamp — renew via re-claim, then restamp); your own stamps never trip close's work-digest fence. Emits a task.criterion event. Stamp is progress; close is the seal.

args.name: worker_id
args.summary: Worker identity that holds the claim (holder-only).

args.name: observed_epoch
args.summary: Claim epoch returned at claim time (same fence as close).

flags.name: criterion
flags.summary: ZERO-BASED index into acceptance_criteria — the first criterion is 0, the second is 1 (do NOT pass a 1-based number). This is the criterion to stamp.

flags.name: criterion-text
flags.summary: REQUIRED with --met (optional with --miss): the criterion's exact stored wording, copied verbatim from acceptance_criteria[N].criterion. It is the off-by-one guard — a --met stamp with NO text is REJECTED (409 criterion_text_required), and one whose text does not match the row at --criterion N is REJECTED (409 criteria_mismatch), instead of silently flipping a neighbour.

flags.name: met
flags.summary: Mark the criterion met. Requires non-empty --evidence.

flags.name: evidence
flags.summary: Concrete proof for --met (gate output, test names, PR) — required, non-empty.

flags.name: miss
flags.summary: Record an honest failed attempt. Appends {note,ts,worker} to the criterion's attempts (5 most recent kept); met never flips.

flags.name: note
flags.summary: What was tried and why it missed — required with --miss, non-empty.

commands.summary: Atomically claim the next executable task (priority order by default).

args.name: phase_id
args.summary: Restrict the claim to tasks under this phase id.

flags.name: order
flags.summary: Optional closure_nearest campaign order: fewest unmet criteria, then oldest, then logical task id.

flags.name: observed_rail_rev
flags.summary: The rail_rev (rail ETag) you last observed for the claimed task's parent rail. When it differs from the claimed task's current rail_rev the response carries a rail_changed notice — advisory, never a gate.

commands.summary: Re-parent a task (rail-l3): move it under another task's rail, or omit new_parent_id to move it to the root. Emits a task.reparented event; the response carries the destination rail_rev + the source from_rail_rev.

args.name: new_parent_id
args.summary: Destination parent task id; omit (or null) to move to the root.

commands.summary: Stage a task between the thought/backlog states — the sanctioned lifecycle-transition verb. `state` is the target: considering | researching | open. Enforces the charter-D7 transition-legality table for those targets: considering⇄researching; considering|researching→open; open→considering; the terminal/blocked reopen edges done→open, cancelled→open, blocked→open, in_progress→open; same→same. (The false-done reopen recipe DEPENDS on reopening a done task — it legitimately re-enters the ready backlog via stage, KEEPING its claim; no epoch machinery.) Writes content.engagement {object,holder,ts,note} on →considering/researching and clears it on →open; emits a task.staged event. done is reached ONLY through `bp task close`, in_progress ONLY through `bp task claim`, kills go through close (→ cancelled); an illegal transition (e.g. → done) is a 422 naming from,to. NO epoch fence — thought is not contended work.

args.name: state
args.summary: Target lifecycle state: considering | researching | open.

flags.name: object
flags.summary: What the thought is ABOUT: research | build. Written into content.engagement on a →considering/researching stage (defaults to research); ignored on →open. An invalid value 400s.

flags.name: note
flags.summary: Free-text note stamped into content.engagement.note on a thought-target stage.

flags.name: worker
flags.summary: The agent/worker owning the thought, stamped into content.engagement.holder.

commands.summary: Heartbeat a held claim: write the now-line (what you're doing right now) AND renew the lease (epoch bump + ts refresh) in one atomic write. No epoch arg — pulse survives fence bumps; a lost lease (reaped/released/closed) is 409 not_holder, never a silent re-claim. Boards render claim.now with its ts so a stale pulse reads stale.

args.name: worker_id
args.summary: Worker identity that holds the claim.

flags.name: now
flags.summary: The now-line text (required, max 500 bytes), e.g. "warm-up pinned, rerunning".

flags.name: criterion
flags.summary: Optional acceptance_criteria index this pulse is working on (boards spin that lock).

commands.summary: The fleet roster: every listener with online/offline computed server-side (offline iff now - last_seen > ttl_s; missing last_seen = offline, fail closed) plus each worker's current in_progress task.

flags.name: dataset
flags.summary: Dataset to read the roster from (defaults to production).

commands.summary: Listener presence heartbeat: upsert this worker's listener row (first beat registers it; every later beat is one zero-row atomic write). last_seen is server-stamped — send ttl as data, never a timestamp.

args.name: worker
args.summary: Worker identity beating (the unique presence key).

flags.name: status
flags.summary: Self-declared state: idle | working | blocked.

flags.name: ttl
flags.summary: Self-declared staleness budget in seconds (default 120).

flags.name: agent
flags.summary: What runs the session: claude-code | codex | custom.

flags.name: scope
flags.summary: What the listener works on (repo, area, project).

flags.name: capacity
flags.summary: Capacity for routing. A JSON object string is validated + stored structured, e.g. '{"size_class":"heavy","slots_total":2,"slots_free":1,"budget":5.0}' (size_class: light | standard | heavy | xl); a plain string is a legacy free-form hint, e.g. "1 task".

flags.name: dataset
flags.summary: Dataset to write the listener row into (defaults to production).

commands.summary: Operator triage: tickets waiting on you, oldest-waiting first (status=open).

flags.name: limit
flags.summary: Max tickets to return.

commands.summary: Show one ticket thread (operator detail: subject, status, messages).
Operator answer (flips status to answered — the key-holder's move). --close answers and closes in one write.

flags.name: close
flags.summary: Close the ticket in the same write (answer + close).

commands.summary: Close a ticket (status=closed, done).
Mint a named ticket key + print the forwardable handoff card (raw key once + curl quickstart).

args.name: name
args.summary: Human label for the key-holder (e.g. "Gyldendal — Kari").

commands.summary: List ticket keys (name, state, last-used).
Rotate a key's secret (same identity + history, new raw key).
Pause a key (403 on use; reversible via unpause — the thread and its history survive).
Unpause a paused key (use resumes; same identity, thread and history intact).
Revoke a key (indistinguishable from missing = 401 on use).
